rules: Family follows the ink, not the frame: point-marker panels on the unitless -40..40 frame read scatter, panels whose ink is a polygon subdivision of the disc read map-or-plan-view, and labelled nodes joined by drawn edges read node-link-network [geometry.family].
Hexagon geometry drawings of the cellular scheme are schematics even when they sit beside real numbers, because they carry no plotted data values [geometry.family].
Every repeater-coordinate table is a full grid, so rule_style is boxed; Table 4, which prints one rule under the header and separates rows by shading, is booktabs [table.rule_style].
Row shading, not rules, tells the coordinate tables apart from the two glossary tables: the former alternate shaded rows, the latter do not [table.zebra].

A table that runs past its page keeps one record: the caption-bearing region is the table, later fragments are excluded as split-across-pages, and `continued` carries the flag while rows counts the whole table [table.continued].

A table caption sits above its body and directly under the previous exhibit's last row, so caption position is above for every table and below for every figure, including Figure 15 whose caption is printed at the top of the next page [caption.position].

Where the geometry pass measured a parent table and its interior cells separately, the interior rectangles are the table's own diagram cells: they are excluded as fragment-of-other instead of being counted as a composite panel [geometry.panel_count].
Captions broken up by the typesetter are quoted as the longest run of printed lines that is still contiguous page text, which is why Figure 14 is quoted short [caption.verbatim].
Section paths come from the printed heading order, not the extracted heading index, because axis tick numbers on pp. 19-23 are indexed as headings [place.section_path].
Prose introduces most exhibits with a direct reference and occasionally inside brackets, so lead_pattern is direct except where the reference is parenthetical [mention.lead_pattern].
